fr.elements: Main Residence; Detached Structure; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Open Green Space; Patio Area; Perimeter Fencing; Access Drive; Dense Vegetation
fr.considerations: Multiple Structures; Dense Vegetation; Limited Rear Access; Single Access Point
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responding units confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the access drive entry clearly so crews arriving under low-visibility or nighttime conditions can locate the single access point without delay.
• Keep the access drive clear of parked vehicles and moveable objects so responding units can reach both structures without repositioning.
• Trim dense vegetation along the access drive to maintain clear sightlines and enough width for emergency vehicles to pass through without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure so crews can move between the two buildings on foot without obstruction.
• Post the detached structure address or unit identifier visibly from the access drive so crews can distinguish between the two structures on arrival.
• Keep a gate, door, or opening in the perimeter fencing accessible from the street side to allow crews to reach the rear of the property on foot when vehicle access is not possible.
• Keep any rear gate unlocked or secured with a breakaway lock so crews are not blocked from reaching the limited rear access area.
• Trim vegetation along the perimeter fencing line so crews can follow the fence quickly to locate gates and move around the property.
• Clear a staging area near the access drive large enough for crews to set down equipment without entering dense vegetation or crossing into landscaped areas that may slow movement.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Adequate Vegetation Separation; Open Terrain; Single Access Route; Limited Rear Access
wildfire.recommendations:
• Thin trees in the cluster nearest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees close to the structure to reduce the path fire could take from the ground up into the tree canopy.
• Trim shrubs and other vegetation that is directly against or touching the exterior walls of the structure.
• Clear dead branches, leaf litter, and dry plant material that has accumulated under trees near the structure.
• Keep scattered trees separated from one another where their branches overlap or nearly touch near the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches, overgrown vegetation, and debris along its full length.
• Mark the driveway entrance clearly so it is easy to locate under low visibility or smoky conditions.
• Pull back any vegetation along the sides of the driveway that narrows the travel lane or blocks a vehicle's line of sight.
• Clear a path around the rear of the structure wide enough for a person to move through quickly, since rear access is limited.
• Remove any wood piles, stored materials, or movable flammable items stored against or close to the structure.
